newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50-$1 -private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50-$1 -private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Monday were seen $1.00 per cwt higher on outlooks for strong packer demand and light marketings, livestock dealers said.
Gains also were seen spurred by the market's further assimilation of Thursday's news that Taiwan banned all pork shipments because of an outbreak of foot and mouth disease.

Taiwan is the biggest supplier of pork to Japan, supplying it with nearly half of its pork imports. Taiwan's departure from the world, market, estimated by some Taiwanese industry sources to last at least six months, opens the door for a significant increase in U.S. pork sales to Japan.

Top prices for Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to plants could range from $49.50 to $50.00 and top prices hogs at Illinois plants could range from $49.00 to $49.50, sources in those areas said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices at the plant could range $48.50 to $49.50.
Cash hog prices also were seen supported by light marketings as producers hold back hogs, they said.
"We've got some guys who are absolutely sitting tight on their hogs because they're going to wait and see what happens (with prices)," one eastern Corn Belt packer buyer said.
